WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    c.customer_unique_id AS cust_uid,
    CAST(o.order_purchase_timestamp AS DATE) AS purch_date,
    CAST(EXTRACT(year FROM CAST(o.order_purchase_timestamp AS TIMESTAMP)) AS INTEGER) AS yr
  FROM orders o
  JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp IS NOT NULL
),
cust_year AS (
  SELECT yr, cust_uid, COUNT(*) AS orders_cnt
  FROM base
  GROUP BY yr, cust_uid
),
year_counts AS (
  SELECT
    yr,
    COUNT(*) AS total_customers,
    SUM(CASE WHEN orders_cnt > 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS repeat_customers
  FROM cust_year
  GROUP BY yr
),
year_orders AS (
  SELECT yr, COUNT(*) AS total_orders
  FROM base
  GROUP BY yr
),
ordered AS (
  SELECT
    yr,
    cust_uid,
    purch_date,
    LAG(purch_date) OVER (PARTITION BY yr, cust_uid ORDER BY purch_date) AS prev_date
  FROM base
),
intervals AS (
  SELECT
    yr,
    DATE_DIFF('day', prev_date, purch_date) AS days_between
  FROM ordered
  WHERE prev_date IS NOT NULL
),
median_intervals AS (
  SELECT yr, median(days_between) AS median_days_between
  FROM intervals
  GROUP BY yr
)
SELECT
  yc.yr AS year,
  yc.total_customers,
  yc.repeat_customers,
  ROUND((yc.repeat_customers * 100.0) / NULLIF(yc.total_customers, 0), 2) AS pct_repeat,
  ROUND(yo.total_orders * 1.0 / NULLIF(yc.total_customers, 0), 2) AS avg_orders_per_customer,
  mi.median_days_between
FROM year_counts yc
LEFT JOIN year_orders yo ON yo.yr = yc.yr
LEFT JOIN median_intervals mi ON mi.yr = yc.yr
ORDER BY yc.yr;
